name: Dagaari Dioula
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Anttila, Arto & Adams Bodomo. 1996. Stress and tone in Dagaare. Rutgers Optimality Archive.
sources.note: The one work explicitly on stress in the Dagaare cluster; describes Central Dagaare (Ghana, sout2789), so it applies to daga1272 only if Glottolog's Dagaari-dialect classification is right — worth reading to know what a Dagaare-internal stress claim looks like.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record daga1272 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Classification Atlantic-Congo > Gur > Oti-Volta >.. > Dagaari > Central > Southern Dagaari > Dagaari Dioula; only two sources: Soumbougma 1989 (phonology, 70 pp.) and Manessy 1975 (wordlist, 7 pp.); subclassification comment cites Kropp Dakubu 2005.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Dagaari Dioula language' (redirects to 'Dagaare language'), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Treats dgd as one of three Ethnologue Dagaare varieties, 'Dagaari Dioula (Burkina Faso, influenced by the unrelated Dioula language)'; phonology/tone section ('tonal language with a two-level tone system with a downstep high tone') is about Dagaare generally (Ghanaian sources), not this variety; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ali, Mark, Scott Grimm & Adams Bodomo. 2021. A dictionary and grammatical sketch of Dagaare. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.5154710
sources.note: Sister variety only (Central Dagaare, Ghana; sout2789): text contains no mention of Dioula/Jula/dgd at all, so it does not cover this language. On prosody it says 'Dagaare is a register tone language with two levels of tone, high and low, and a downstepped high unit' (sketch, phonology section); no stress statement; bibliography cites Anttila & Bodomo 1996 'Stress and tone in Dagaare' (ROA).
